sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F1][F8][F145].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 5.2% in FY2024 before rebounding 9.8% in FY2025 [D201][D236].
The FY2024 decline reflected lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues at FPL [P35].
The FY2025 rebound came from higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel recovery [P21].
FPL supplied 70.5% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% growth [D271][D273][D236].
FPL's revenue rose on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues [P21].
NEER's results grew on higher earnings from new wind, solar and battery storage investments [P26].
Operating income grew 9.9% a year against revenue's 7.7%, while net income compounded at only 0.4% [F146][F145][F147].
Operating costs grew 0.2pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 10.0% [D257][D249].
The FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sat above the 30.3% window median and well above the 15.5% FY2021 low [F24][D300][D298].
The margin rose 0.3pp in FY2025, with D&A at 25.5% of revenue [D247][D224].
Depreciation and amortization rose $951 million, mainly on higher storm cost amortization and plant in service [P16].
In FY2025 net margin of 26.5% sat 5.6pp below the 32.1% operating margin, as other expense of $3.75 billion and a -17.7% tax rate weighed [F40][F24][X64][D226].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025, against a 2.11x FY2021 level [F64][F32][D227][D87].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% in FY2025, and operating cash flow was 48.4% of revenue [D241][D225].
The shift from over-recovery to under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million [P19].
Capex is not separately disclosed in the pack; investing outflow of $23.9 billion dwarfed operating cash flow [F72][F64].
Net cash of -$92.2 billion in FY2025 was -357.4% of revenue, against a -228.4% peer median [D231][D232][D315].
That ranks at the 0th percentile of the four-peer utilities group, and long-term debt grew 23.7% in FY2025 [D314][D245].
The current ratio of 0.60x is the window high but still below 1.0x [F128][D305].
Dividends of $4.68 billion were paid while debt issued of $23.4 billion far exceeded the $10.3 billion repaid [X82][X90][X98].
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x every year, at 0.60x in FY2025 [F128][R1].
For a regulated utility with committed credit lines this is a working-capital convention rather than a liquidity crisis, but it leaves little buffer [R1].
Net cash fell for seven straight years into net debt of $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D9][D21][D56][D91][D126][D161][D196][D231][R2].
Debt-funded growth is the model here, but the 18.8% long-term debt CAGR against 6.9% equity growth steadily thins the cushion [F156][F157][R2].
The effective tax rate moved -23.3pp in FY2025 to -17.7%, driven by clean energy tax credits at NEER [D226][D191][P11][R4].
A negative tax rate flatters net income and is unlikely to persist at this level, so the 26.5% net margin overstates underlying earnings power [F40][R4].
Whether the FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% holds above the 30.3% window median in the FY2026 10-K [F24][D300].
Whether net debt stays above the FY2025 level of $92.2 billion or reverses in the FY2026 10-K [D231].
Whether operating cash flow conversion recovers above the FY2025 1.83x toward the FY2021 2.11x in the FY2026 10-K [D227][D87].
